items.title: The GDP report is expected to show economic growth. Could it affect the midterms?
items.excerpt: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Stacey Vanek Smith, host of the podcast Everybody's Business from Bloomberg BusinessWeek, about what signs of economic growth could mean for the midterms.

items.title: Support for Trump among white evangelicals has plummeted, polls reveal
items.excerpt: Three new polls suggest that President Trump is losing ground among white evangelicals. What explains this drop — and will it affect the midterm elections?

items.title: Hackers expose the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
items.excerpt: A group of hacktivists calling themselves Distributed Denial of Secrets, said the unmasking of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors was fair play, given the government's lack of transparency.

items.title: Judge denies the Justice Department's bid to stop processing California ballots
items.excerpt: While the judge rejected the Department of Justice's unprecedented demand in California, the case isn't over yet and will likely be appealed.

items.title: A breakthrough for the group on the trail of Chinese hackers
items.excerpt: Chinese government hackers are secretly burrowing into critical networks using creative new methods.

items.title: Democrats are hoping Latino voters swing back their way in Arizona and elsewhere
items.excerpt: This year, Democrats are hoping Latino voters swing back to them. Particularly in Arizona, where the party is trying to flip to some competitive congressional races.

items.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
items.excerpt: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

items.title: How a lifelong Republican came to lead the data center battle in Ohio
items.excerpt: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

items.title: Senate candidates built up massive campaign war chests with out-of-state donations
items.excerpt: In several competitive U.S. Senate contests, candidates have built healthy campaign accounts with out-of-state donations. But the messages to those donors is very different from the one back at home.

items.title: Why many student voters have a right to choose where to register to vote
items.excerpt: Student voters studying outside their hometown have a right to choose where they register to vote. Advocates say a Montana legal fight is a reminder of a misunderstanding of those students' rights.

items.title: Here's how Democrats in Congress are preparing for election fraud claims
items.excerpt: Congressional Democrats are working with good governance groups to create an action plan for any potential claims of election fraud.

items.title: Former DOJ official on judge blocking Trump's D.C. golf course renovation
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with author and former Justice Department official Sarah Isgur about the block on President Trump's renovation of the East Potomac Golf Course.

items.title: Iran war and cost-of-living take center stage in Virginia congressional race
items.excerpt: High prices and long deployments are shaping this year's race in Virginia's Second Congressional District. The area with deep Navy ties has been a kind of political bellwether.

items.title: Minnesota becomes battleground as political clashes shape Senate race
items.excerpt: Minnesota has become a flashpoint in the political dispute between President Trump and Democrats. Clashes over immigration and recent accusations of voter fraud are spilling into the U.S. Senate race.

items.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
items.excerpt: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.

items.title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
items.excerpt: Democrats are still holding a slight edge with Election Day a week away, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. And, Israelis are casting their votes in an election that could change leadership.

items.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
items.excerpt: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy.

items.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
items.excerpt: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.

items.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
items.excerpt: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.

items.title: How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump
items.excerpt: Democrats in Congress are bracing for what they fear could be meddling by President Trump or his allies with the results of this year's midterm elections.

items.title: Data centers are a hot-button issue for Ohioans as midterms near
items.excerpt: In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot-button issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.

items.title: As campaign rhetoric escalates, Michigan voters say they're burned out
items.excerpt: From college football tailgates to conversations in Ann Arbor, Michigan voters tell NPR they're worried about everyday costs, frustrated with the two-party system and increasingly reluctant to discuss politics openly.

items.title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
items.excerpt: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.

items.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
items.excerpt: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.

items.title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
items.excerpt: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.

items.title: Redistricting isn't playing out how the GOP hoped. And, Brazil's Lula wins 4th term
items.excerpt: Republicans are spending millions on the midterms, and they still may not win districts drawn to favor them. And, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in a stunning political comeback.

items.title: Political consultant on the impact of Republicans' gerrymandering efforts
items.excerpt: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with political consultant Mike Madrid about how Republicans' gerrymandering efforts have backfired.

items.title: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan
items.excerpt: President Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States.

items.title: Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them
items.excerpt: Republicans redrew Congressional district lines to try to tilt the midterms in their favor. But now they are facing expensive and competitive races they had hoped to outmaneuver.

items.title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
items.excerpt: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.

items.title: Politics chat: The polls show a Democratic sweep in the midterms. Can you trust them?
items.excerpt: If you look at the few truly competitive seats, polls show a more complicated picture of momentum toward the Democratic Party in midterm House races. For the Senate, Republicans are on defense.

items.title: Democrats see an opportunity to tilt Pennsylvania's state legislature their way
items.excerpt: Statehouse elections this fall could swing the balance of power in state capitals. In Pennsylvania, Democrats could take control of what has been a divided legislature.

items.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
items.excerpt: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.

items.title: Independent candidates sense a moment in the West. Democrats are hoping they're right
items.excerpt: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.

items.title: The rise of the economic populist: What voters want from both parties this year
items.excerpt: A new kind of economic populism is surging in both parties this year as voters search for a political party that can solve growing concerns about financial stability.

items.title: Week in Politics: Ramaswamy's Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate
items.excerpt: Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.

items.title: This decade has been missing its big-impact midterm
items.excerpt: Every other decade over the past hundred years has produced at least one midterm that made a big difference in Congress and in national politics more broadly.

items.title: At a Texas high school football game, fans offer a glimpse into evolving politics
items.excerpt: We talk with voters at a Texas high school football game at the tailgate, in line at the concession booth and in the stands to hear about the issues that matter to Texans this cycle.

items.title: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
items.excerpt: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.

items.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
items.excerpt: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

items.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
items.excerpt: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.

items.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
items.excerpt: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.

items.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
items.excerpt: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

items.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
items.excerpt: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

items.title: Trump's midterm campaign tour stops in Iowa
items.excerpt: Republicans are facing a tough fight in Iowa. President Trump's campaign tour stopped in the state in hopes of rallying voters.

items.title: Gen Z candidates in both parties aim to tackle high housing costs
items.excerpt: Young candidates who rent or live with parents say their generation is "in the thick" of the country's housing affordability crisis. They argue this gives them new energy to solve it for everyone.

items.title: What's behind the early voting surge? It's more than voter enthusiasm, expert says
items.excerpt: Nearly 21 million Americans have voted early in the midterms. MIT political scientist Charles Stewart explains what's driving the surge and why it may not mean higher overall turnout.

items.title: Trump must sit for a deposition in his BBC defamation lawsuit, judge rules
items.excerpt: A magistrate judge orders President Trump to sit for a deposition in a case he's brought against the BBC for defamation.

items.title: Trump's attacks on the press have become a war
items.excerpt: The New York Times reported that the Trump Administration is considering physically moving the White House press corps out of the White House.

items.title: Federal judge restricts DHS field operations looking for noncitizen voters
items.excerpt: The judge found the department's field operations to identify noncitizens who voted likely violated the Voting Rights Act, which bars voter intimidation.

items.title: U.S., Israel may attack Iran post-elections. And, SpaceX and Tesla consider merging
items.excerpt: The U.S. and Israel are planning for a possible post-elections attack on Iran, an anonymous source tells NPR. And, Elon Musk considers merging his companies SpaceX and Tesla.

items.title: Trump's redistricting gave Republicans a head start, now it goes to the voters
items.excerpt: President Trump, seeking to reshape the voting map, prompted a rare wave of mid-decade redistricting that gave Republicans a boost for holding the House. But the voters will determine if it works.

items.title: Farm country has beef with Trump as midterms approach
items.excerpt: President Trump's attempts to bring beef prices down has potentially backfired politically in several key states.

items.title: Trump merchandise stores are closing: 'He has peaked'
items.excerpt: At least four Trump merchandise stores have closed this year. Store owners say with Trump in his final term, there isn't as much to fire up his consumer fan base and sales have softened.

items.title: High health costs squeeze workers, even if you have good insurance through a job
items.excerpt: About 157 million Americans get their health insurance through work. A survey of employers shows a moderate price uptick this year, but workers still say health costs are a top concern.

items.title: Backlash from attack ad upends Ohio gubernatorial race
items.excerpt: An ad from Republican Vivek Ramaswamy's {vih-vaik rah-mah-SWOM-eez} campaign for governor shows his opponent's mother calling her a liar, amid accounts by Democrat Amy Acton of an abusive childhood.

items.title: Political communications expert discusses Vivek Ramaswamy's controversial ad
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political communications expert Jacob Neiheisel from the University of Buffalo about Vivek Ramaswamy's controversial ad.

items.title: Kara Swisher on Elon Musk: 'He's unelected, unaccountable, enormously wealthy'
items.excerpt: As Elon Musk considers merging Tesla and SpaceX, tech journalist Kara Swisher examines his business strategy, growing political influence and power over the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Citing 'challenges,' AIPAC halts endorsements and direct contributions to candidates
items.excerpt: The pro-Israel lobbying group and influential political donor announced it would no longer endorse candidates or give directly to campaigns, instead mobilizing its members to give individually.

items.title: The Justice Department begins notifying counties where it wants to monitor elections
items.excerpt: The department has long deployed election monitors, but the Trump administration's unprecedented steps to try to wrestle control over elections have led to new concerns about DOJ monitoring this year.

items.title: California gas prices have long plagued Democratic candidates. This year is different
items.excerpt: Gas prices in California continue to be the highest in the nation, but the war in Iran has given California Democrats a rare opportunity to turn the tables on the issue.

items.title: Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad features mother of Amy Acton, who alleges childhood abuse
items.excerpt: A campaign ad by Republican candidate for Ohio governor Vivek Ramaswamy includes the mother of Democrat Amy Acton. Acton says they've been estranged since she was abused as a child by her stepfather.

items.title: Candidates lock in for final sprint in Texas U.S. Senate race
items.excerpt: What issues are bringing individuals to the polls in this key race that could decide the balance of power in Congress? What last minute push is being made by the campaigns?

items.title: Poll: Voters want Congress to be a check on Trump, trust Democrats more on issues
items.excerpt: A new poll shows record support for Democratic congressional candidates ahead of the midterms, as voters feel the party is better attuned to handling their top issues.

items.title: Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
items.excerpt: The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

items.title: How Trump's attacks on voting system integrity might affect upcoming elections
items.excerpt: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains Trump's interference in the midterms, including threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they strike alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.

items.title: Why local officials are feeling 'on edge' as election day approaches
items.excerpt: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.

items.title: Supreme Court upholds pause on Trump's anti-trans prison policy
items.excerpt: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration has to continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons as litigation on efforts to change the policy continues.

items.title: Trump leans into unprecedented power ahead of midterm elections
items.excerpt: Less than two weeks before the election, Trump continues to crash through barriers that he wouldn't dare cross in his first term.

items.title: DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises
items.excerpt: The Justice Department's "likely" noncitizen voter list in California is "unreliable," according to officials. And, the United Nations reports a major increase in U.S. climate pollution.

items.title: Why Republicans frustrated with Trump's policies continue to support the party
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Bloomberg politics columnist Ron Brownstein what motivates Republicans angry with the Trump administration to continue voting for the Republican party.

items.title: Trump to campaign for Sen. Darline Graham despite disagreement on Russia sanctions
items.excerpt: President Trump is expected to campaign with Sen. Darline Graham on Wednesday even as the two are not in agreement on how to best pressure Russia to end the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Some on DOJ's 20,000 "likely" noncitizen list in Calif. appear to be U.S.-born
items.excerpt: Election officials in Los Angeles County say their preliminary analysis of the federal government's list of 20,000 "likely" noncitizens registered to vote in California shows the list is "unreliable."

items.title: Supreme Court recusals stop music case in its tracks, strike warning note
items.excerpt: A publishing dispute has highlighted the issue of recusals by Supreme Court justices. The justices largely police themselves.

items.title: Supreme Court recusals over books raise questions about policy
items.excerpt: A publishing dispute has highlighted the issue of recusals by Supreme Court justices. We take a look at the court's policy and its impact.

items.title: Beef producers could play a big role in this year's midterm elections
items.excerpt: Trump's policies have complicated his support among beef producers, a key constituency in states where tight Senate races could sway control of the body.

items.title: DOJ charges 28 with voting crimes. And, TikTok ignored staff's child safety concerns
items.excerpt: The Justice Department has charged 28 people in California with voting crimes as Election Day nears. And, TikTok staff raised child safety concerns with executives, who failed to act, court records show.

items.title: A new poll shows what voters are thinking 2 weeks out from Election Day
items.excerpt: Midterm election day is just over two weeks away. What are some numbers on the mind of voters?

items.title: DOJ charges 28 in California with voting crimes as election tensions escalate
items.excerpt: The DOJ also filed an emergency request in federal court to stop California from processing ballots returned by people on the voter rolls the federal government says are "likely noncitizens."

items.title: Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course
items.excerpt: The Trump administration wants to turn a historic public golf course into championship links. Despite a judge's order, hundreds of trees were cut down to make way for the renovation.

items.title: Judge hears latest arguments on White House renovation of Washington golf course
items.excerpt: A federal judge grills government lawyers on Trump's golf course plan

items.title: Between the coasts, populist Democrats see room to reclaim lost ground in red states
items.excerpt: In parts of the Great Plains and Midwest, Democrats are betting that harnessing anger at corporate power and both parties might succeed when voters believe the economy and government are not working.

items.title: 2026 midterms could be the most expensive on record. And, Macron condemns protests
items.excerpt: More than $15 billion has been raised in this year's midterm elections. And, France's president is condemning the violent protests erupting across the country.

items.title: Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., on Trump waiving sanctions on Russia
items.excerpt: NPR's Leila Fadel asks Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia about President Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia.

items.title: The real reason it's going to take a while to know who won in some midterm races
items.excerpt: Hint: It's not only because California counts slowly.

items.title: Michigan's Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed campaigns in GOP stronghold
items.excerpt: Michigan's Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is campaigning in the GOP stronghold of Michigan's Upper Peninsula, an area that hasn't voted for a Democrat in Congress in over a decade.

items.title: Democrats — and Elon Musk — continue to dominate midterm campaign fundraising
items.excerpt: Democratic candidates are on offense with fundraising, and Republican super PACs continue to play defense heading into the final weeks of the midterm.

items.title: What does a White House press secretary do?
items.excerpt: Katie Zacharia's short time as White House press secretary has brought renewed attention to the high-profile role.

items.title: Congress reacts to executive order exempting Russia from economic sanctions
items.excerpt: NPR's Eric McDaniel reports on how Congress has reacted to President Trump's executive order exempting Russia from economic sanctions.

items.title: Greensboro, NC students protest the absence of early voting sites on campus
items.excerpt: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to North Carolina A&T student Shia Rozier about disappointment with early voting sites in Greensboro.

items.title: What role does the White House Press Secretary play in the Trump era?
items.excerpt: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks Adm. John Kirby, who had spokesperson roles in the Obama and Biden administrations, about the utility of the role of the White House Press Secretary.

items.title: Politics chat: Zelenskyy on Trump, Democrats bring in the money for midterms
items.excerpt: From Russia to AI to Iran, President Trump has taken political stances that put him at odds with much of the electorate.

items.title: Trump suspends federal diesel taxes to help farmers, but states issue warnings
items.excerpt: President Trump's executive order suspending federal taxes on diesel is aimed at helping farmers but it's more complicated than it sounds and states are warning drivers they may owe taxes later.

items.title: With an ad aimed at Trump, this Republican exposed GOP angst about Latino voters
items.excerpt: Rep. María Elvira Salazar filmed an ad warning the president that he's "gone too far" on immigration. It reflected concern among some Republicans that their gains with Latino voters could be at risk.

items.title: Fraud, affordability and Trump policies drive friction in Minnesota Senate debate
items.excerpt: The major party candidates for Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat faced off in an hourlong debate Friday on MPR News with fraud, affordability and fallout from the Trump administration's policies as key points of friction.

items.title: Week in Politics: Trump's Russian diesel deal update; why the DOJ is suing California
items.excerpt: We look at where things are in the deal President Trump says he made to import Russian diesel, plus the reason why the Justice Department is suing California.

items.title: Trump promised a swing district blitz. He's going to a lot of very red states
items.excerpt: President Trump's midterm travel blitz ahead of Election Day includes several red states he won easily 2 years ago, showing the electoral landscape is more challenging for Republicans.

items.title: Here's what experts say about the civilian intervention in the Bend school shooting
items.excerpt: An armed bystander stopped a shooting at a school in Bend, Ore. We talk with experts about how rarely an armed civilian ends an attack like this and how gun rights groups are responding.

items.title: Katie Zacharia is out as press secretary, White House says
items.excerpt: Katie Zacharia is "transitioning out" of her role as press secretary, according to a White House official not authorized to speak on the record, marking a stunning turn of events for the spokeswoman.

items.title: Trump casts doubt on press secretary's future
items.excerpt: Katie Zacharia's first official day was on Monday.

items.title: Amid talk of public execution, public opinion on death penalty is split
items.excerpt: A majority of Americans support the death penalty for people convicted of murder, but support becomes more divided when questions vary.

items.title: Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in UK after Palestinian Action support
items.excerpt: The Irish author said her books can no longer be sold in the UK after she pledged the royalties to a banned pro-Palestinian group.

items.title: Teen kills 4 at Oregon school. And, DOJ sues California over alleged noncitizens
items.excerpt: A teen opened fire at an Oregon elementary school, leaving three kids and one teacher dead. And, the Justice Department is suing California over alleged noncitizen voters.

items.title: Do Americans own the president's papers? Appeals court to weigh in
items.excerpt: The administration says papers created in the White House belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people. The case could ultimately end up at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.

items.title: Why some Gen Z voters who backed Trump now regret their decision
items.excerpt: A focus group of eight Gen Z Trump voters reported feeling unhappy or disappointed with the state of politics, with some going as far as to say they regret supporting him in 2024.

items.title: Suspicious mailings to election officials, congressional offices under investigation
items.excerpt: The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are looking into the mailings, some of which included an unidentified powdery white substance.

items.title: America's historic preservation law is in peril, advocates say. Here's what's at stake
items.excerpt: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.

items.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space
items.excerpt: The Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel says Musk and Bezos each want to colonize the moon, mine its resources and launch thousands more satellites. He says their only real competition is each other.

items.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
items.excerpt: The Trump administration provided few details about its process for canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments — even as the next stage of the anti-fraud effort is underway.

items.title: For some Christians, Hegseth's plan for public execution fits a biblical mandate
items.excerpt: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.

items.title: These swing voters regret voting for Trump and it's influencing their midterm choices
items.excerpt: Some key voters in Georgia say deep frustration and disappointment with President Trump are motivating their election plans just weeks before Election Day.

items.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
items.excerpt: The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct.

items.title: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns following misconduct allegations
items.excerpt: President Trump has forced out his ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle. She faced allegations of misconduct before and during her tenure at the U.S. Embassy in Athens, which she has denied.

items.title: In Kansas, a newly-competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
items.excerpt: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.

items.title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
items.excerpt: For many election cycles, civil rights groups and political parties have fanned out to monitor polling places, but the charged midterm environment has many organizations stepping up efforts this year.

items.title: Former White House ethics lawyer on Kimberly Guilfoyle's alleged ethics violations
items.excerpt: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with former chief White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter about the ethics allegations facing former U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, who resigned Tuesday.

items.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign among corruption allegations
items.excerpt: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been asked to resign as US ambassador to Greece following allegations that she sought payment from a Trump donor in exchange for access to administration officials

items.title: Why does Pete Hegseth want to livestream an execution?
items.excerpt: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has proposed livestreaming the execution of a man convicted of the 2009 attack on Fort Hood. Some scholars say the idea is rooted in his religious background.

items.title: Conservative super-lawyer squares up for his latest Supreme Court argument
items.excerpt: Paul Clement, a Republican, has racked up dozens of wins at the Supreme Court since his days as George W. Bush's solicitor general. Recently, he's been challenging some Trump administration policies.

items.title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
items.excerpt: Six Democratic and six Republican senators wrote a letter calling on President Trump to withdraw from his recent deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

items.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
items.excerpt: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

items.title: Government spent millions on Trump ads. And, federal agents raid Ilhan Omar's home
items.excerpt: The government is using millions of taxpayers' dollars on pro-Trump ads, even after the president said this would not happen. And, federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home.

items.title: Win or lose, independent candidates want to meet voters in the middle
items.excerpt: Nearly 200 independent candidates in more than 100 congressional races are trying to prove there's an alternative to the two party system — even though the chance of winning is very low.

items.title: Should states force cities to build cheaper houses? Voters here will decide
items.excerpt: Voters in Massachusetts will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. A growing number of states are doing the same to help ease a housing shortage.

items.title: Polls are a snapshot, and other helpful things to remember during the midterm elections
items.excerpt: With Election Day just a few weeks away — and millions of votes already cast — midterm polls are everywhere. While polling can be a helpful tool to understand the electorate, it's not a crystal ball.

items.title: Montana ballot measure could undo ruling on corporate spending in state politics
items.excerpt: Montana voters will have a chance to speak out on the boom of corporate and anonymous money in politics that has been the result of the Citizens United court ruling.

items.title: New White House press secretary a "devoted fan" of Trump and MAGA
items.excerpt: Katie Zacharia worked for one of Trump's companies and raised her profile appearing on conservative-leaning talk shows. She also amplified right-wing conspiracy theories. Now she'll be the president's chief spokesperson.

items.title: Government spent $10 million on pro-Trump ads after president said super PAC would fund
items.excerpt: Nearly $22 million in taxpayers funds has been spent to air the ads, with nearly half spent after Trump promised to fund what the White House calls public service announcements through his super PAC.

items.title: Agents search Rep. Omar's D.C. home; DOJ says it's part of criminal investigation
items.excerpt: The Justice Department says the search is part of an "ongoing federal investigation," while Omar calls it "an attempt to target political enemies."

items.title: Democratic senator talks Trump's Russian diesel deal
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks to Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire about President Trump's deal for Russian diesel and his claim of an "energy ceasefire" that did not materialize.

items.title: Political strategist on how Trump's personal grievances could affect the GOP
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political strategist and former senior Republican congressional adviser Rina Shah about how President Trump's personal grievances and projects are affecting the chances of GOP candidates in the upcoming election.

items.title: Republican strategist on how Trump's personal grievances could affect the GOP
items.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Republican strategist Rina Shah about how President Trump's personal grievances and projects are affecting the chances of GOP candidates in the upcoming election.

items.title: Trump struggles to show voters he's focused on the cost of living
items.excerpt: With a deal to import millions of tons of diesel fuel from Russia, President Trump is struggling to show voters that he is focused on the cost of living ahead of the midterms.

items.title: NEWSBRIEF: TRUMP RUSSIA UKRAINE, TRUMP PRIORITIES, SAUDI AIRPORT STRIKES
Texas' 15th Congressional District provides clues to state's Latino vote
items.excerpt: The 15th Congressional District runs from the east of San Antonio all the way down into the Rio Grande Valley. This majority-Latino district provides a window into the Latino vote in Texas.

items.title: Justice Department investigates TV networks, citing possible anti-trust violations
items.excerpt: The move escalates Trump's fight with the press amid court battle over barring CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House.

items.title: Politics chat: Trump announces fuel deal with Russia. What does it mean for sanctions?
items.excerpt: President Trump announced a deal to import Russian fuel to the U.S. We look at what this means for the sanctions he recently signed off on against Russia, as well as the U.S.'s support for Ukraine.

items.title: In one of the country's most competitive districts, a Democrat tries to keep her seat
items.excerpt: In a highly competitive Washington congressional race, the incumbent Democrat has angered part of her party base and the Trump-backed Republican challenger faces backlash against the party in power.

items.title: Reshaped civil rights mission at Justice Department transforms its work, workforce
items.excerpt: Harmeet Dhillon has pushed out hundreds of longtime attorneys, replaced many with inexperienced ideological allies, and used the division's enforcement powers to pursue the president's agenda.

items.title: Trump's economic strategy resemble similar policies in East Asia
items.excerpt: Much of the Trump administration's economic policy has been inspired by successful industrial policies successful in East Asia, including those of competitor, China. Will those policies work in the U.S.?

items.title: U.S. imposes sweeping sanctions on International Criminal Court
items.excerpt: The U.S. has announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowing to dismantle the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal.

items.title: Week in Politics: Hegseth's livestream backlash; Greece ambassador Guilfoyle scandal
items.excerpt: Bipartisan blowback on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plans to livestream a military execution, plus a scandal involving Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US Ambassador to Greece.

items.title: On the ground in Ohio's 9th District: The battleground shaping next month's midterms
items.excerpt: Ohio is a critical battleground in next month's midterms elections. NPR's Scott Simon traveled to the state's 9th Congressional District to hear from voters about their priorities.

items.title: After losing ground with Latino voters, Democrats are turning to influencers for help
items.excerpt: Democrats are hoping to win back Latino voters who have soured on both parties. They hope Latino content creators will bridge the gap.

items.title: Trump says U.S. to get diesel from Russia, relaxing pressure on Moscow to ease prices before midterms
items.excerpt: Trump says the U.S. will obtain diesel from Russia, relaxing years of U.S. pressure on Moscow, to combat prices before midterms. He said he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call.

items.title: Trump's Affordable Suit
items.excerpt: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with New York Times fashion reporter Jacob Gallagher about President Trump's apparent choice to wear a suit from the budget menswear chain Jos. A. Bank.

items.title: Billionaire, also the U.S. president, spotted in Jos. A. Bank suit
items.excerpt: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with New York Times fashion reporter Jacob Gallagher about President Trump's apparent choice to wear a suit from the budget menswear chain Jos. A. Bank.

items.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
items.excerpt: The Trump administration's effort to return Ahmed Soliman to the U.S. come after an Arizona judge said his deportation violated due process.

items.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
items.excerpt: If you're using the U.S. Postal Service to return a ballot close to Election Day, officials recommend getting it postmarked at a post office to avoid getting caught up in mail processing changes.

items.title: Republican congressman tries to outrun a potential blue wave in New York toss-up seat
items.excerpt: Rep. Mike Lawler, R-NY, is in a tight race for re-election in a toss-up district that could help determine control of Congress in November.

items.title: 25 years later an Afghan couple looks back at the invasion
items.excerpt: Twenty-five years ago this week, the U.S. invaded Afghanistan. For StoryCorps, one Afghan couple offers an account of their experience after the invasion and eventual U.S. withdrawal.

items.title: Trump's War in Iran in spotlight ahead of midterms
items.excerpt: After President Trump slapped down reports that he is considered renewed strikes against Iran ahead of the midterms, the politics of the war he started are in the spotlight.

items.title: A Congressman wants his colleagues to pledge to accept election results
items.excerpt: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.Y., on a bipartisan pledge he is co-leading to assure that fellow House members accept midterm elections results.

items.title: White House correspondent April Ryan reflects on reporting while under attack
items.excerpt: Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs. Her new book is Notes on a Blacklash.

items.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
items.excerpt: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

items.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
items.excerpt: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

items.title: Toss-ups, triage and targets: How to read the wide-open 2026 House map
items.excerpt: Both parties are spending heavily in roughly 60 House districts — where Trump won by an average of nine points in 2024 — that could be key to deciding control of the chamber, an NPR analysis finds.

items.title: How 'Musk' director Alex Gibney became a critic
items.excerpt: A trove of documents and interviews with people close to tech billionaire Elon Musk reveal a damning picture of his rise as one of the world's richest and most powerful men.

items.title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club
items.excerpt: President Trump said he wants to develop one of his Florida golf courses into a presidential retreat where his successors can spend quiet weekends, describing it as "sort of a Camp David."

items.title: Trump approved the military's 1st firing squad execution since WWII. Why now?
items.excerpt: The Pentagon says Nidal Hasan will be executed by firing squad in December at Fort Hood, where he killed 13 people in 2009. The announcement came days after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

items.title: She got Trump's $500 check for health insurance. To her, it's a 'political stunt'
items.excerpt: As checks from President Trump for health costs hit millions of mailboxes, a poll shows Americans don't trust Republicans on healthcare. Experts doubt it will move the needle and say it is likely illegal.

items.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
items.excerpt: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

items.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
items.excerpt: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.

items.title: Dems have edge in midterms, poll shows. And, Paramount-Warner Bros. merger to close
items.excerpt: Polls are showing that Democrats have a clear advantage heading into the midterms, but that doesn't tell the whole story. And, today, a mega merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. is set to close.

items.title: What voters in 6 key states could tell us about the 2026 midterms
items.excerpt: Morning Edition is heading to Maine, Texas, North Carolina, Georgia, Ohio and Michigan to hear what voters say is shaping their choices ahead of the midterm elections.

items.title: A history of presidents naming things after themselves (It's short. They rarely do)
items.excerpt: While Trump pushes to get his name on the Kennedy Center and other public sites, history shows that sitting presidents have almost always avoided putting their brands on government assets.

items.title: With 4 weeks to go, a look at where November's big races stand
items.excerpt: Election Day is four weeks away and people are already voting in the 2026 midterms. Where do things stand in the big races across the country?

items.title: What challenges lie ahead for the Democratic Party as midterms approach
items.excerpt: Democrats are feeling optimistic ahead of the midterms, but what challenges remain? NPR's A Martinez asks Devan Barber, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.

items.title: Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections
items.excerpt: President Trump has repeatedly called for Disney's ABC to fire late night comedian Jimmy Kimmel, for mocking him. Trump has also routinely denounced ABC's The View, accusing it of being unfair.

items.title: Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey's new Pentagon roles raise ethics worries
items.excerpt: Musk's company, SpaceX, and Luckey's company Anduril, could potentially benefit from recommendations made in the study about future autonomous weapon systems.

items.title: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
items.excerpt: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.

items.title: People are asking ChatGPT to help them decide how to vote in the midterms
items.excerpt: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.

items.title: Trump names national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new AI czar
items.excerpt: Trump said Clayton will lead the White House's new "Super Intelligence Force," which will coordinate government engagement with artificial intelligence.

items.title: Politics chat: Midterm polls, Senate races, Trump in Texas
items.excerpt: As polls come out with increasing frequency closer to the midterm election, how much credence should voters give them? Meanwhile, President Trump continues campaigning for GOP candidates.

items.title: Latter-day Saints women turn away from scandal-plagued Republican candidate in Arizona
items.excerpt: Arizona Republican candidate for Congress Mark Lamb has been accused of sexual misconduct while sheriff. His controversy is turning many voters away as Democrats see an opportunity in the red seat.

items.title: Week in Politics: Inflation pressure; war in Iran and effect on midterm elections
items.excerpt: We look at how some concerning economic indicators as well as the ongoing war in Iran might affect the midterm elections.

items.title: How high-profile scandals are shaping key contests ahead of the midterms
items.excerpt: Scandals could be shaping several races in the midterm elections, particularly in places where even small margins can change the outcome.

items.title: California voters to decide on controversial one-time tax on billionaires
items.excerpt: California voters will decide whether the state will charge a one-time tax on billionaires. The idea that has split Democrats and labor unions.

items.title: The Supreme Court faces another term jam-packed with controversy
items.excerpt: The Supreme Court term opens on Monday with big test cases on religion, guns and climate change. Plus, the emergency docket keeps popping.

items.title: As Trump's proposed arch looms over D.C., protesters pin their hopes on the midterms
items.excerpt: Democratic lawmakers, veterans and concerned citizens gathered in Memorial Circle to protest the arch Trump wants to build there. Their hopes lie primarily in a lawsuit and next month's midterms.
